summary: After the January 2026 US operation that captured Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, AI-generated images and videos and recycled old footage spread widely on social media. NewsGuard counted seven fabricated or misrepresented visuals with over 14 million views on X.
technical_summary: Cheap generative image and video tools produced realistic fake scenes of Maduro in custody and of Venezuelans celebrating. Fact-checkers detected one image through Google's SynthID watermark. Platform recommendation and resharing amplified the content before community notes or fact-checks appeared.

summary: The EU fined Google 2.4 billion euros for favoring its own shopping comparison service over rivals in search results. An EU court later upheld the fine and rejected Google's argument that its algorithm changes improved search quality.
technical_summary: Google changed its search ranking algorithms in Europe so its own comparison shopping service was placed above competitors. The ranking system optimized for the company's own commercial interest rather than result quality, producing anti-competitive effects that regulators and the General Court found unjustified.

summary: A Moscow-based network called Pravda mass-publishes pro-Kremlin falsehoods so AI chatbots absorb them. A NewsGuard audit found ten leading chatbots repeated its false narratives about a third of the time.
technical_summary: The network floods the web with millions of aggregated, translated articles to poison search results and crawler-collected data (so-called LLM grooming). Chatbots that retrieve or train on this data then repeat the laundered claims, treating the sources as credible.

sector.quote: By flooding search results and web crawlers with pro-Kremlin falsehoods, the network is distorting how large language models process and present news and information

summary: A Facebook video showed Kenyan journalist Jeff Koinange apparently endorsing a gambling app. Fact-checkers found it was a deepfake built from a real Citizen TV report, with his voice and mouth movements altered.

summary: Gannett paused its use of an AI tool for high school sports articles after stories with unfilled template text, repetition and awkward phrasing went viral and were mocked online.
technical_summary: An automated text-generation service published sports reports in several Gannett papers. Outputs contained unfilled placeholders, repeated phrases and lacked key details, indicating insufficient quality control before publication. Gannett paused the experiment across markets and the vendor corrected the problems.

summary: A Xiaomi SU7 Ultra crashed in Chengdu, China, and caught fire. Bystanders could not open the electronic doors and the driver died. Police suspected drunk driving, but the case renewed scrutiny of automated driving and door-handle design.
technical_summary: After a high-speed collision the car's electrically powered door handles reportedly failed, trapping the driver as the vehicle burned. Reports also cite automated-driving concerns, but police attributed the crash to suspected impaired driving, so the role of driver assistance is unconfirmed.

summary: A New Brunswick legislator read aloud a chatbot's leftover instructions during a speech in the Legislative Assembly, apparently without noticing. Residents criticized him online and some called for his resignation.
technical_summary: A draft speech prepared with a large language model still contained the chatbot's meta-text about producing a more natural, flowing version. It was not removed before delivery, showing unreviewed use of generated text in an official setting.

summary: Investigators say scammers are using AI chatbots, voice cloning and synthetic identities to run more convincing frauds, including executive impersonation and fake IDs. Banks are adopting AI defenses, but reported losses to scams keep rising.
technical_summary: Generative AI removes tell-tale errors from scam messages, clones voices and produces fake faces and documents that pass identity checks. The tools let fraudsters scale targeting and personalize lures, making detection harder for banks and consumers.

summary: Greek police say a fraud ring cloned the voices of victims' relatives with AI to make impersonation calls convincing, then collected money and valuables from victims. Two collectors were arrested, and total proceeds are estimated above one million euros.
technical_summary: Callers posing as utility or telecom staff asked victims to call a relative, recorded that relative's voice sample, and used an AI voice-cloning tool to recreate it. A second call then used the cloned voice to reassure the victim before collectors took cash and valuables.
